events.title: The Agricultural Revolution
events.description: Humans begin transitioning from hunter-gatherer lifestyles to permanent settlements and farming.

events.title: Invention of the Wheel
events.description: The earliest known use of the wheel occurs in Mesopotamia (modern-day Iraq).

events.title: Invention of Writing
events.description: Sumerians develop Cuneiform, one of the earliest systems of writing.

events.title: Completion of the Great Pyramid of Giza
events.description: Built as a tomb for Pharaoh Khufu, it remains the oldest of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.

events.title: Code of Hammurabi
events.description: One of the earliest and most complete written legal codes is established in Babylon.

events.title: First Ancient Olympic Games
events.description: The first recorded athletic competition is held in Olympia, Greece.

events.title: Founding of Rome
events.description: The legendary founding of the city of Rome by Romulus and Remus.

events.title: Athenian Democracy Established
events.description: Cleisthenes introduces a system of political reforms in Athens, the basis of modern democracy.

events.title: Alexander the Great Begins Conquests
events.description: The Macedonian king crosses the Hellespont to begin his campaign against the Persian Empire.

events.title: Unification of China
events.description: Qin Shi Huang becomes the first emperor of a unified China and begins building the Great Wall.

events.title: Assassination of Julius Caesar
events.description: The Roman dictator is stabbed by senators on the Ides of March.

events.title: Eruption of Mount Vesuvius
events.description: The volcano erupts, burying the Roman cities of Pompeii and Herculaneum in ash.

events.title: Fall of the Western Roman Empire
events.description: The Germanic chieftain Odoacer deposes the last Western Roman Emperor, Romulus Augustulus.

events.title: The Hijra
events.description: The Prophet Muhammad and his followers migrate from Mecca to Medina, marking the start of the Islamic calendar.

events.title: Charlemagne Crowned Emperor
events.description: Pope Leo III crowns Charlemagne as Holy Roman Emperor in Rome.

events.title: Battle of Hastings
events.description: William the Conqueror defeats King Harold II, beginning the Norman Conquest of England.

events.title: The First Crusade Begins
events.description: European Christians set out to reclaim the Holy Land from Muslim rule.

events.title: Completion of Angkor Wat
events.description: The massive Hindu temple complex is completed in present-day Cambodia.

events.title: Genghis Khan Unites Mongols
events.description: Temüjin is proclaimed Genghis Khan, leader of the Mongol Empire.

events.title: Magna Carta Signed
events.description: King John of England signs the 'Great Charter,' establishing that the monarch is not above the law.

events.title: Marco Polo Sets Out for China
events.description: The Venetian merchant begins his famous journey to the court of Kublai Khan.

events.title: Black Death Arrives in Europe
events.description: The bubonic plague begins spreading across the continent, eventually killing roughly 30-60% of the population.

events.title: Invention of the Printing Press
events.description: Johannes Gutenberg develops the movable-type printing press, revolutionizing information sharing.

events.title: Fall of Constantinople
events.description: The Ottoman Empire captures the capital of the Byzantine Empire, marking the end of the Middle Ages.

events.title: Columbus Reaches the Americas
events.description: The Italian explorer, sailing for Spain, lands in the Bahamas, thinking he has reached Asia.

events.title: Leonardo da Vinci Paints the Mona Lisa
events.description: The Italian Renaissance polymath begins work on his most famous portrait.

events.title: The Protestant Reformation Begins
events.description: Martin Luther reportedly nails his 95 Theses to the door of the Castle Church in Wittenberg.

events.title: Magellan's Circumnavigation Begins
events.description: Ferdinand Magellan sets sail on the first expedition to sail around the world.

events.title: Fall of the Aztec Empire
events.description: Spanish conquistador Hernán Cortés captures Tenochtitlan.

events.title: Defeat of the Spanish Armada
events.description: An English fleet defeats the invasion force sent by King Philip II of Spain.

events.title: Establishment of the Tokugawa Shogunate
events.description: Ieyasu Tokugawa is appointed Shogun, beginning a long period of peace and isolation in Japan.

events.title: Galileo Observes Jupiter's Moons
events.description: Galileo Galilei uses a telescope to discover four moons orbiting Jupiter, challenging the geocentric model.

events.title: Mayflower Compact Signed
events.description: Pilgrims sign the first governing document of Plymouth Colony.

events.title: Construction of the Taj Mahal Begins
events.description: The Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan commissions the mausoleum for his favorite wife.

events.title: Great Fire of London
events.description: A major conflagration sweeps through the central parts of London.

events.title: Newton Publishes Principia Mathematica
events.description: Isaac Newton lays out his laws of motion and universal gravitation.

events.title: Start of the Industrial Revolution
events.description: The transition to new manufacturing processes begins in Great Britain.

events.title: U.S. Declaration of Independence
events.description: The Thirteen Colonies declare themselves free from British rule.

events.title: Storming of the Bastille
events.description: Parisian citizens storm the medieval fortress and prison, sparking the French Revolution.

events.title: Haitian Revolution Begins
events.description: A successful slave revolt begins against French colonial rule in Saint-Domingue.

events.title: First Smallpox Vaccine
events.description: Edward Jenner performs the first vaccination against smallpox.

events.title: Napoleon Crowns Himself Emperor
events.description: Napoleon Bonaparte is crowned Emperor of the French at Notre-Dame Cathedral.

events.title: Battle of Waterloo
events.description: Napoleon's final defeat at the hands of the Duke of Wellington and Gebhard Leberecht von Blücher.

events.title: Voyage of the HMS Beagle Begins
events.description: Charles Darwin sets sail on a five-year journey that will lead to his theory of evolution.

events.title: Samuel Morse Patents the Telegraph
events.description: The invention revolutionizes long-distance communication.

events.title: The Year of Revolutions
events.description: A series of political upheavals occurs throughout Europe.

events.title: Publication of On the Origin of Species
events.description: Charles Darwin introduces his theory of natural selection.

events.title: American Civil War Begins
events.description: Confederate forces fire on Fort Sumter, South Carolina.

events.title: Suez Canal Opens
events.description: The artificial waterway connecting the Mediterranean and Red Seas is officially opened.

events.title: First Successful Telephone Call
events.description: Alexander Graham Bell speaks to his assistant, Thomas Watson.

events.title: Edison Demonstrates the Light Bulb
events.description: Thomas Edison gives his first public demonstration of the incandescent light bulb.

events.title: Berlin Conference
events.description: European powers meet to regulate colonization and trade in Africa.

events.title: First Modern Olympic Games
events.description: The first international Olympic Games of the modern era open in Athens.

events.title: Wright Brothers' First Flight
events.description: Orville and Wilbur Wright achieve the first controlled, sustained flight of a powered aircraft.

events.title: Sinking of the RMS Titanic
events.description: The 'unsinkable' ship hits an iceberg and sinks in the North Atlantic.

events.title: Assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand
events.description: The event in Sarajevo triggers a chain of events leading to World War I.

events.title: The Russian Revolution
events.description: The Bolsheviks led by Lenin seize power in Russia.

events.title: League of Nations Founded
events.description: The first intergovernmental organization to maintain world peace is established.

events.title: The Jazz Singer Released
events.description: The first 'talkie' feature film marks the end of the silent film era.

events.title: Discovery of Penicillin
events.description: Alexander Fleming discovers the first antibiotic substance.

events.title: Black Tuesday Stock Market Crash
events.description: The Wall Street crash signals the beginning of the Great Depression.

events.title: World War II Begins
events.description: Germany invades Poland, leading Britain and France to declare war.

events.title: D-Day Landings
events.description: Allied forces invade the beaches of Normandy, France.

events.title: Atomic Bombing of Hiroshima
events.description: The first atomic bomb used in warfare is dropped by the United States.

events.title: United Nations Founded
events.description: The UN is established to prevent future world conflicts.

events.title: Independence of India and Pakistan
events.description: British rule in India ends, resulting in the partition of the subcontinent.

events.title: Universal Declaration of Human Rights
events.description: The UN General Assembly adopts a milestone document in the history of human rights.

events.title: First Ascent of Mount Everest
events.description: Sir Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay reach the summit of the world's highest peak.

events.title: Brown v. Board of Education
events.description: The U.S. Supreme Court rules that racial segregation in public schools is unconstitutional.

events.title: Launch of Sputnik 1
events.description: The Soviet Union launches the first artificial satellite into orbit.

events.title: Construction of the Berlin Wall Begins
events.description: East Germany begins building the wall to prevent citizens from fleeing to the West.

events.title: I Have a Dream Speech
events.description: Martin Luther King Jr. delivers his famous speech during the March on Washington.

events.title: Apollo 11 Moon Landing
events.description: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin become the first humans to walk on the moon.

events.title: Richard Nixon Resigns
events.description: The 37th U.S. President becomes the first to resign from office due to the Watergate scandal.

events.title: Star Wars Released
events.description: George Lucas's space opera changes cinema and pop culture forever.

events.title: IBM PC Released
events.description: The launch of the Model 5150 helps popularize the personal computer.

events.title: Chernobyl Disaster
events.description: A catastrophic nuclear accident occurs at the Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant in Ukraine.

events.title: Fall of the Berlin Wall
events.description: The wall is opened, leading to the reunification of Germany and the end of the Cold War.

events.title: Nelson Mandela Released
events.description: The anti-apartheid leader is freed from prison after 27 years.

events.title: First Web Page Published
events.description: Tim Berners-Lee publishes the first website on the World Wide Web.

events.title: Rwandan Genocide Begins
events.description: A mass slaughter of Tutsi in Rwanda begins, lasting for 100 days.

events.title: Handover of Hong Kong
events.description: Britain transfers sovereignty of Hong Kong to the People's Republic of China.

events.title: September 11 Attacks
events.description: Terrorist attacks on the World Trade Center and the Pentagon change global security.

events.title: Election of Barack Obama
events.description: The first African American President of the United States is elected.

events.title: COVID-19 Pandemic Declared
events.description: The World Health Organization declares the global outbreak a pandemic.
